standard.title: Create informative and imaginative texts
standard.description: create spoken, written and multimodal, informative and imaginative texts using appropriate vocabulary, expressions, grammatical structures, and some textual conventions
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can locate and process information in familiar texts (AC9LS8EC04) and interact using modelled language (AC9LS8EC01–03). They have not yet created extended spoken, written or multimodal texts in the target language for specific purposes and audiences.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students create spoken, written and multimodal texts (informative and imaginative) in the target language, selecting appropriate vocabulary, expressions and grammatical structures, and applying some textual conventions appropriate to the text type, purpose and audience.

nodes.label: Structuring a text for purpose and audience
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify the structural conventions of a familiar target language text type and apply them in their own text production.
nodes.minimum_width: Produce one text in the target language that follows a recognisable structural convention (e.g. a presentation with greeting, introduction and sequenced ideas; a narrative with beginning, middle and end).
nodes.typical_width: Prepare and produce texts across at least two formats (e.g. a spoken presentation and a written informative text); apply structural conventions appropriate to each text type and identify audience for each text.
wider: Compare the structural conventions of equivalent text types (e.g. a presentation, a notice, a story) in the target language and in English — identify where conventions align and where they diverge
Produce a bilingual text for a mixed-language audience — consider how structural and linguistic choices change when the audience changes
nodes.hinge_reason: Text structure awareness is the precondition for all subsequent text creation. Students who produce language without any structural frame produce utterances, not texts — they cannot meet the descriptor's demand for textual conventions or demonstrate audience awareness, both of which require a sense of the text as a whole.

response_modes.reason: Students need explicit instruction in the structural conventions of target language text types before they can apply them. Annotated model texts, structural frameworks and co-constructed exemplars help students see text organisation as a deliberate choice, not a default.

success_criteria: Produces a text with a recognisable structure appropriate to the chosen text type (not just a list of sentences)
Can identify the intended audience for the text and explain at least one structural choice that reflects that audience

nodes.label: Selecting vocabulary and expressions
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can select vocabulary and expressions appropriate to the topic, purpose and audience of their text rather than defaulting to the first known word.
nodes.minimum_width: Demonstrate at least two deliberate vocabulary or expression choices in a target language text — can explain why each choice suits the purpose or audience.
nodes.typical_width: Select vocabulary and expressions consciously for appropriateness to topic, purpose and register; use set phrases and idiomatic expressions where appropriate; avoid over-reliance on direct translation from English.
wider: Revise a draft text by substituting more precise or contextually appropriate vocabulary — compare the original and revised versions and discuss the effect of the changes
Build a personal vocabulary journal or resource that organises known vocabulary by topic, purpose and register rather than only by translation

response_modes.reason: Deliberate vocabulary selection requires a repertoire — students who know only one word for each concept cannot make choices. Building vocabulary breadth across topic areas and registers is the precondition for meaningful selection.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Vocabulary repertoire at Y7-8 directly predicts the richness of text production in Y9-10. Investing in varied vocabulary exposure across topics and registers now creates the raw material for the more complex text creation demanded in AC9LS10EC06.
success_criteria: Can identify and explain at least two deliberate vocabulary choices in their own text
Does not default entirely to direct English-to-target-language substitution — uses at least some target language expressions or set phrases

nodes.label: Applying grammatical structures in text creation
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can apply familiar grammatical structures accurately enough in a target language text to convey intended meaning to an audience.
nodes.minimum_width: Produce a text in which the grammatical structures required for the text type (e.g. present tense verbs, basic agreement, interrogative forms) are applied with sufficient accuracy to convey meaning.
nodes.typical_width: Apply a range of grammatical structures (tense, agreement, sentence types) in both informative and imaginative texts; self-correct common errors during drafting; connect ideas using basic connectives.
wider: Review and revise a peer's draft text — identify grammatical errors that affect meaning and suggest corrections with explanations
Experiment with grammatical variation (e.g. changing sentence type, adding detail with prepositions or adjectives) to observe how it changes the effect of a text

response_modes.reason: Grammatical accuracy in text production is a fluency issue at Y7-8 — students typically understand the structures but apply them inconsistently under the cognitive load of text creation. Focused drafting-and-revision cycles rather than isolated grammar exercises are the most productive practice structure.

success_criteria: Produces a text in which grammatical structures are accurate enough for the meaning to be understood by an audience unfamiliar with the student's intent
Can identify and self-correct at least one grammatical error in their own draft during revision

nodes.label: Creating imaginative texts
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can create an imaginative text (narrative, role-play, performance, visual story) in the target language that communicates ideas for an intended audience.
nodes.minimum_width: Produce one imaginative text in the target language with a recognisable communicative intent and at least one deliberate creative choice (e.g. a character detail, an event sequence, a humorous or dramatic element).
nodes.typical_width: Create imaginative texts across a range of formats (narrative, role-play, performance, illustrated story, script); make deliberate creative choices about character, situation and effect; present imaginative work to an audience.
wider: Collaborate with a peer on a jointly-authored imaginative text — negotiate plot, character and language choices across the collaboration
Experiment with creative techniques from target language literary or cultural traditions (e.g. story structure conventions, poetic forms, performance styles)

response_modes.reason: Imaginative text creation integrates structural awareness, vocabulary selection and grammatical application from nodes 1–3 into a purposeful creative act. The teaching investment is in supporting students to see creative constraint (text type, audience, purpose) as enabling rather than limiting.

success_criteria: Produces a complete imaginative text in the target language with a recognisable intent and structure
Can explain at least one deliberate creative choice in their text and its intended effect on the audience
